title: The Wild Veil
premise: Jude Ashgrove, a scribe indentured to the Temple of the Quiet Ledger, lives in the Veiled Valley where magic has been sealed out for three generations. When prayers begin reaching the old gods again, Jude discovers their own bloodline was the price of the sealing — and that the covenant's thirteenth moon-turn is expiring, letting wild magic bleed through unchecked. Hunted by temple inquisitors and courted by desperate gods, Jude flees the valley for the first time, gathering the scattered oath-bearers of the broken covenant. In the end, Jude must choose between restoring the old seal and forging a new covenant that binds gods and mortals as equals — paying for it with their name, their debt, and their place in the only home they've ever known.
about_author: Oscar Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned parish records before turning to fantasy. They write about debt, faith, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet Jude copying tithes in the Temple of the Quiet Ledger, bound by a family debt they can never repay. A beggar's prayer at the temple door is answered — impossibly — by a voice of rain. Emotional beat: quiet longing beneath routine, and the first crack in an ordered world.

chapters.title: What the Rain Remembered
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The answered prayer spreads through the valley; more miracles follow, each tied to forgotten god-names Jude finds scratched in the ledger margins by a predecessor. The High Scribe orders all marginalia burned. Emotional beat: dread mixed with fascination as Jude secretly copies the names first.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Notch
chapters.summary: Wren, a young acolyte and skeptic, POV. Wren discovers the valley's boundary stones each bear twelve notches — and one stone shows a fresh thirteenth. The elders deny everything. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your teachers have been lying.

chapters.title: Ink and Interrogation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Inquisitor Halvard Vey arrives from the capital, elegant and terrifying, investigating the miracles. He questions Jude about the burned pages — and reveals he knows Jude's grandmother signed the original sealing. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The God of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A minor god — Ash-of-the-Threshold, small, ragged, half-forgotten — appears in the scriptorium at night and claims Jude's blood can open the old covenant. It asks nothing yet, only leaves a token: a key made of moth-wing. Emotional beat: wonder laced with suspicion.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Boundary
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with Wren along. Accused of heresy after Vey finds the copied names, Jude flees the valley at night, crossing the boundary stones — and feels magic touch them for the first time. Wren chooses exile over silence. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of leaving home forever.

chapters.title: The Road That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Outside the valley, geography is unreliable; roads move, and the pair are nearly lost until a hedge-witch named Marisol shelters them and explains the covenant: thirteen moons, thirteen oath-bearers, most dead or scattered. Emotional beat: grief for the world's complexity, and first belonging among strangers.

chapters.title: A Court of Crows and Contracts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The god of crows, Kessivar, offers Jude protection in exchange for a written contract — Jude's scribe skills make them valuable to gods who cannot hold pens. Jude signs carefully, learning the law of the wild realm. Emotional beat: empowerment through literacy in a world of power.

chapters.title: The Oath-Bearer's Grave
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The trio finds the first oath-bearer's tomb desecrated — Vey's agents got there first, harvesting bones for a counter-ritual. Marisol reveals she is herself a failed oath-bearer, marked and cast out. Emotional beat: mourning, and resolve hardened by failure.

chapters.title: Moonturn Rising
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Under the waxing moon, wild magic surges: crops bloom and rot in hours, a river speaks. Jude's blood-mark burns, showing them visions of the original sealing — their grandmother weeping as she signed. Emotional beat: horror at learning their inheritance was a betrayal.

chapters.title: What Vey Wants
chapters.summary: Halvard Vey's POV. Vey believes the gods are parasites and the sealing was mercy; he intends to renew it permanently using harvested relics — with himself as sole arbiter. His conviction is sincere. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist's logic.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Beneath a flooded chapel, the group recovers the Covenant Stone, but Wren must bargain with a river-god who demands a memory as toll. Wren gives up their memory of the temple — of home. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the price of passage.

chapters.title: Ash-of-the-Threshold's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The small god finally names its price: to reforge the covenant, an oath-bearer must surrender their name entirely — becoming the living hinge between realms. It has waited centuries because no one would pay. Emotional beat: the weight of a choice that cannot be unmade.

chapters.title: Thirteen Names, Twelve Voices
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The company gathers the surviving oath-bearers — a disgraced knight, twin shepherds, a god-touched child — but one seat stays empty: the traitor who helped seal the gods away still lives, hidden. Emotional beat: fragile hope assembling against odds.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Confession
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The twelfth oath-bearer is revealed: the High Scribe of Jude's own temple, who followed them out. She confesses the sealing was meant to protect mortals from devouring gods — and that Vey's version will enslave them instead. Emotional beat: moral ambiguity deepening; no clean side.

chapters.title: Siege at the Standing Stones
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vey's inquisitors, armed with relic-magic, assault the gathered circle at the standing stones on the twelfth moonturn. The knight falls holding the line; the Covenant Stone cracks. Emotional beat: costly victory, the circle broken but not destroyed.

chapters.title: The Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Captured by Vey, Jude is offered freedom from their ancestral debt if they help renew the seal. In the cells beneath his camp, Jude reads the true terms of their grandmother's contract — and finds a flaw, a mercy-clause she hid in the ink. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into cunning hope.

chapters.title: Ink Against Iron
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Using the hidden clause, Jude voids their own debt and turns Vey's ritual circle against itself, escaping with the stolen relics as the thirteenth moon begins to rise. Emotional beat: triumph of the scribe — words as weapons.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the boundary stones under the full thirteenth moon, the circle reconvenes amid Vey's last assault. The old covenant fails; the realms begin to tear. Emotional beat: apocalyptic pressure, everything staked on one act.

chapters.title: The Nameless Hinge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude speaks the new covenant — gods and mortals bound as equals, neither sealed nor sovereign — and pays its price: their name, erased from every record, memory, and tongue. Even this account cannot hold it. Emotional beat: transcendent loss; identity surrendered so others may belong.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Unnamed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The realms settle into uneasy balance; Vey, broken by witnessing the new covenant's fairness, surrenders his relics. Wren returns to the valley carrying a letter no one can read — signed only with a moth-wing mark. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Ensemble close, mostly Wren and Marisol. The valley's boundary stones now bear thirteen notches and an open gate; the temple becomes a school where gods and mortals study together. On the threshold each dawn, someone leaves ink and paper for a visitor whose name no one remembers — but everyone feels. Emotional beat: belonging redefined; an ending that is also a beginning.
